title: A Scientist Tests Tattoo Ink That Can Disappear and Come Back
summary:
Tattoos are usually permanent. But engineers at the University of Colorado Boulder are working on a new kind of tattoo ink that can be seen only some of the time. Its color changes depending on whether it is hit by ultraviolet (UV) light or ordinary visible light.

The team described the ink in a study published this month in the journal Matter & Light. They tested it in the lab on silicone and pig skin. One of the inventors, nanoscientist Carson Bruns, also tattooed his own leg with it. He called testing on himself "almost a tradition." Bruns earlier created a product called "Magic Ink" that turns magenta in UV light.

The new ink comes in three colors: yellow, blue and magenta. It works using the same ideas behind glasses lenses that darken in sunlight. Each dye is made of tiny beads of acrylic glass. Inside the beads are special chemicals called photochromes, which absorb certain kinds of light. When the dye absorbs UV light, it becomes clear and seems to vanish. When it later absorbs visible light, the chemicals change back, and the original color returns.

Bruns tattooed his leg over about 12 months using different color combinations. All of them responded to light as the team expected. The ink also kept working for more than two years.

The researchers hope the ink could be more than a neat trick. In the future, a version might help doctors make temporary marks on the skin during radiation treatments, so they can aim accurately.

For now, the ink is only for laboratory use. More safety tests are needed before anyone else can use it.
why_it_matters: Light-switching inks show how chemistry can create materials that change on command, which could someday help doctors mark skin accurately without a permanent tattoo.

background_read: A tattoo is made by placing tiny drops of ink under the top layer of skin, which is why most tattoos last for many years.
Light comes in many kinds, and ultraviolet light is one our eyes cannot see, while visible light is the kind we see as colors.
Some chemicals can switch between two forms when they absorb certain light, and that switch can change what color they look.
Before any new product is used on people, scientists must run safety tests to make sure it does not cause harm.
